correctness.rationale: Independently recomputed from scratch (own GF(2) multiply/mod, own pair-weight tallies, own Griesmer/Singleton routines; no reuse of candidate code paths). All three headlines divide x^n+1, have claimed (k,dH,d2,spectra): (8,3,g=0x33,dH=4,d2=6,spec {0:1,6:4,8:3}); (12,5,g=0xbd,dH=4,d2=8,spec {0:1,8:9,9:16,12:6}); (14,3,g=0xb97,dH=8,d2=12,const pair-weight {0:1,12:7}); sums equal 2^k. Griesmer formula 3n>=sum_{i<k}ceil(2d/2^i) matches Luo Thm 1 at q=2,b=2; verified d_G equals d2 in each case (S(d)=21<=24, S(7)=25>24; S(8)=31<=36, S(9)=37>36; S(12)=42<=42, S(13)=46>42) and d_S=n-k+2 gives gap_S=1 in all three, so Griesmer is strictly stronger than Singleton (not MDS). Non-membership in Luo families A/B verified arithmetically (both require n=2^t-1; 8,12,14 are not of that form). Exhaustiveness verified: per-n divisor counts 3,4,3,8,7,8,7,8,3,24,3,26,31 sum to 135 rows, sum 2^k=140806 matches logged dual-tally asserts; CSV spectra/counts consistent. (31,5,24) reference directly reconstructed from h=x^5+x^2+1 via g=(x^31+1)/h: dH=16, constant pair-weight 24 (31 words), dG=24. Known A/B members re-found exactly at (3,2,3),(7,3,6),(15,4,12)/(3,3,2),(7,4,5),(15,5,11). Evidence is machine-certified exhaustive enumeration with dual tally plus independent string-based verifier (computational proof), honestly scoped as such; no infinite-family claim. Minor presentation blemishes (cryptic per-length shorthand line in DRAFT 3.3; confusing reciprocal-twin sentence) do not alter any headline number; underlying CSV/JSON are correct.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp/failed-search: Luo et al. arXiv:2401.04941 proves the general b-symbol Griesmer bound (qb-1)n/(q-1)>=sum ceil(q^{b-1}db/q^i) and proposes exactly two distance-optimal families (cyclic (q^k-1)/Delta type and extended-cyclic (n,b,n)-type; at q=2,b=2 families A (2^t-1,t,3*2^{t-2}) and B (2^t-1,t+1,3*2^{t-2}-1)). Headline parameters (8,3,6),(12,5,8),(14,3,12) cannot be members (n not of form 2^t-1) and are not contained or mechanically implied by the bound or the two constructions. Shi-Zhu-Helleseth arXiv:2109.13764 states metric connections and the cyclic b-symbol Griesmer conjecture (k multiple of b) with only Theorems 2.7/3.17 tight examples; no optimal constructions or gap table at surveyed lengths. Singleton-attaining MDS/AMDS symbol-pair work (Li-Ge, Tang-Luo, Chen-Lin-Liu) uses a disjoint optimality notion; headline gap_S=1 proves these are not MDS re-descriptions. Live arXiv searches on 2026-09-08: 'b-symbol Griesmer bound distance-optimal' returns only Luo et al. (1/1); 'symbol-pair Griesmer optimal cyclic' returns no results. No prior third Griesmer-optimal family or short-length Griesmer-gap table found.

value.rationale: Strongest headline judged alone: three rigorously established exact Griesmer-optimal binary cyclic symbol-pair codes outside both known families, each with full spectrum and Singleton gap 1 proving a strictly non-Singleton certificate. Qualifies under the exact-invariant clause: natural object (short binary cyclic b=2 codes) and invariant (b-symbol distance/spectrum/Griesmer gap) motivated before computation by the Shi-Zhu-Helleseth conjecture and Luo bound-sharpness program for overlapping-read channels (Cassuto-Blaum/Yaakobi), values not known or mechanically implied, reusable for future code selection and sharpness points (including constant-pair-weight (14,3,12) and mixed-spectrum (12,5,8)). Not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration: spectra, generators, and gap logs are committed and replayable, and the complete 3<=n<=15 census plus per-length records add benchmark value without being required to rescue the headline.
